title: How Much Money Will GTA 6 Make? What Take-Two's $8B Outlook Says
desc: Take-Two gives no GTA 6-only figure; it guides $8.0 to $8.2 billion in Net Bookings company-wide for its launch year. GTA 6 costs $79.99, or $99.99 Ultimate.
keywords: how much money will gta 6 make, gta 6 revenue, gta 6 sales forecast, how much money has gta 6 made, gta 6 price, gta 6 $80, take-two net bookings, gta 6 pre-orders, gta 6 ultimate edition price, gta 6 pricing market impact
question: How much money will GTA 6 make, and what does its $79.99 price mean for the games market?
cta: Planning a launch at a premium price?
body:
Short answer. Take-Two Interactive, which owns Rockstar Games, does not publish a revenue figure for Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) on its own. What it has said is that it expects $8.0 to $8.2 billion in Net Bookings for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, up 19% to 22% on the $6.72 billion it booked the year before, with GTA 6 launching on November 19, 2026 at $79.99, or $99.99 for the Ultimate Edition. For the October to December 2026 quarter that includes launch, it guides $3.35 to $3.5 billion, roughly double the $1.76 billion of a year earlier.

On 16 November 2026 we read Take-Two's second quarter fiscal 2027 earnings release and the prepared remarks for its November 9, 2026 call, its fiscal 2026 results release and annual report on Form 10-K, the June 2026 pre-order announcement, Rockstar's newswire and support pages, and the PlayStation and Xbox store listings. Analyst figures below are forecasts, named and dated, not results. This is a business explainer. It is not investment advice and says nothing about Take-Two shares.

What Take-Two has said about GTA 6 money

On November 9, 2026, Take-Two reported Net Bookings of $1.60 billion for its fiscal second quarter, the three months to September 30, 2026. That was down 18% from $1.96 billion a year earlier, and, as the call script notes, slightly below its own guidance of $1.62 to $1.67 billion. It kept the full-year outlook of $8.0 to $8.2 billion that it first gave in May 2026.

On pre-orders, the company gave words, not numbers. CEO Strauss Zelnick said in the release that pre-orders were reaching "unprecedented levels", and in the call script that they were tracking "far in excess of our initial expectations". Chief Financial Officer Lainie Goldstein called the level of pre-orders extraordinary. Neither gave a unit count or a dollar figure, so any number you see for GTA 6 pre-order revenue did not come from Take-Two.

Three figures show where the money is expected to land:

  • The launch quarter. Take-Two projects $3.35 to $3.5 billion in Net Bookings for October to December 2026, against $1.76 billion in the same quarter of 2025. By our arithmetic that is 90% to 99% higher, and 2.1 to 2.2 times the quarter just reported.
  • The second half. First-half Net Bookings were $2,987.2 million. Subtracting that from the full-year outlook leaves about $5.0 to $5.2 billion for October 2026 to March 2027, the half that contains the launch.
  • The label split. Take-Two expects roughly 37% of fiscal 2027 Net Bookings from Rockstar Games, 34% from Zynga and 29% from 2K. That is about $3.0 billion for Rockstar, but it covers every Rockstar game, including Grand Theft Auto V, GTA Online and Red Dead Redemption, not GTA 6 alone.

Net bookings in plain words

Net Bookings is Take-Two's own operating measure, and its releases define it as the net amount of products and services sold digitally or sold-in physically during the period, including licensing fees, merchandise and in-game advertising. In plain words, it is the value of what Take-Two sold in a period, counted when the sale happens.

It differs from GAAP net revenue, the accounting figure, mainly because accounting rules can defer part of a sale into later periods. In the September quarter, net revenue was $1.50 billion against Net Bookings of $1.60 billion.

Three details matter when you read GTA 6 numbers:

  • Sold-in is not sold to players. A boxed copy counts when Take-Two sells it in to a store. The 10-K estimates that sell-through to the end player comes about two months after sell-in.
  • The store takes its share first. For sales through Sony's PlayStation Network, Microsoft's Xbox store and Valve's Steam, the 10-K says Take-Two is not the principal and reports revenue based on what it receives from the store. A $79.99 digital copy is therefore not $79.99 in Take-Two's books. It does not disclose the per-copy split.
  • Recurrent consumer spending is the repeat money. Take-Two uses the term for virtual currency, add-on content, in-game purchases and in-game ads. It was 81% of Net Bookings in the September quarter.

The full-year outlook is $1.28 billion to $1.48 billion above fiscal 2026. Take-Two's own explanation, in its May 21, 2026 release, is that fiscal 2027 records would be driven by the November launch of GTA 6.

What analysts forecast, and how to read it

GameSpot reported on November 13, 2026 on a compilation of analyst notes by Investor's Business Daily. These are forecasts:

  • Brian Pitz of BMO Capital Markets forecast 55 million copies in Take-Two's fiscal 2027, including 45 million in the launch quarter. The launch-quarter estimates compiled by Investor's Business Daily stood at 34.2 million.
  • Andrew Marok of Raymond James forecast 50 million copies in fiscal 2027 at a blended average price close to $90.
  • GameSpot also cited Sensor Tower data suggesting early pre-orders leaned toward the $99.99 edition, with a split near 50/50 possible by launch.

Our arithmetic on the Raymond James forecast gives 50 million copies times $90, or $4.5 billion of buyer spending. Do not read that as Take-Two revenue. On PlayStation and Xbox, Take-Two books what the store passes on, not what the player pays, and Take-Two's own guidance for its whole company, every game included, is $8.0 to $8.2 billion for the full fiscal year. We found no named source for the "$3 to $5 billion in the first week" figure that circulates online.

For scale, Take-Two said on September 20, 2013 that Grand Theft Auto V reached more than $1 billion in worldwide retail sales in its first three days, by company estimates. In the November 2026 call script it said Grand Theft Auto V has sold nearly 235 million units, 13 years after release. The 10-K for fiscal 2026 put the figure at over 225 million sold-in.

The price: $79.99, $99.99 and a $20 upgrade

The June 24, 2026 announcement set the standard edition at $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition at $99.99, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. On 16 November 2026 both prices were unchanged on the PlayStation Store and the Xbox Store, which also sells a Grand Theft Auto VI: Ultimate Edition Upgrade for $20.00 as an add-on.

Rockstar's editions page says Standard Edition owners can buy that upgrade separately as a digital add-on. Purchases before November 20, 2026 add the Vintage Vice City Pack, and digital pre-orders came with a free month of GTA+, Rockstar's subscription. Rockstar's newswire opened pre-loading for digital pre-orders on November 10, 2026.

The Ultimate tier matters more than its price suggests. In the call script, Take-Two said it expects recurrent consumer spending to be about level with fiscal 2026 in dollars, which would be 65% of Net Bookings, down from 78%. That assumes strong growth in GTA recurrent spending, largely because it expects robust sales of the Ultimate Edition, which includes add-on content. So Take-Two ties Ultimate Edition sales to recurrent spending, not only to game sales.

What GTA 6 pricing means for the games market

$79.99 is $10 or 14.3% above $69.99. It is not the first $79.99 game: Nintendo lists Mario Kart World at $79.99 on its US store. Other new releases have stayed at $69.99. The same Nintendo store lists Take-Two's own NBA 2K27 at $69.99, and Microsoft's Xbox Wire post for The Outer Worlds 2 carries an editor's note that its standard edition price was revised to $69.99, next to a $99.99 premium edition.

So the market has two signals at once: a $99.99 premium tier appears on both GTA 6 and The Outer Worlds 2, while a $79.99 base price is still a choice publishers make title by title. In our view, GTA 6 is the largest test so far. Take-Two itself lists the ability to maintain acceptable pricing levels on its games among the risks in its forward-looking statements, so even the company treats price as something the market can push back on.

What one launch can settle is narrow. It can show whether buyers accept $79.99 for the next Grand Theft Auto, 13 years after GTA V. It cannot show that buyers will pay the same for a game with less demand behind it, and we found no publisher saying it will follow.

One game and Take-Two's revenue mix

The 10-K says Grand Theft Auto products were 12.4% of Take-Two's net revenue in fiscal 2026, and its five best-selling franchises together were 54.3%. A year with GTA 6 shifts that mix in three ways:

  • More money from game sales. Recurrent spending was 78% of Net Bookings in fiscal 2026 and is guided at 65% for fiscal 2027. By our arithmetic on those rounded shares, full-game and other Net Bookings rise from about $1.5 billion to about $2.8 to $2.9 billion.
  • Rockstar as the largest label. Rockstar is guided at roughly 37% of the year, against 34% for Zynga, its mobile games label, and 29% for 2K.
  • Higher launch costs. Take-Two expects operating expenses for October to December to grow about 21%, mainly for GTA 6 marketing. The call script describes a Netflix premiere for an extended look at the game that drew 31 million people in its first four days, and an NBA "Night In Vice City".

The trade-off is concentration. Take-Two names its dependence on NBA 2K and Grand Theft Auto products as a risk in the cautionary note of its November 9, 2026 release.

What it means for retailers and console makers

Retailers. The physical version is a box with a download code inside, and Rockstar's support page says a disc will not be included. Physical retail and other made up 2% of Take-Two's Net Bookings in the September quarter, against 5% a year earlier, while digital was 98%. The 10-K still calls packaged goods and traditional retailers an important channel for console products for the foreseeable future, so stores sell the moment and the gift box, but the product is a code.

Console makers. At launch Take-Two lists GTA 6 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and Rockstar's newswire names Xbox Cloud Gaming as the route for Xbox One owners. Take-Two's outlook assumes continued growth in the installed base of PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Sony and Microsoft each accounted for more than 10% of Take-Two's fiscal 2026 net revenue, and its five largest customers together for 80.6%, and on digital copies Take-Two books only what their stores pass on. We found no hardware sales forecast tied to GTA 6 from Sony or Microsoft, so we do not give one.

Lessons for launching at a premium price

Few businesses will launch anything this size, but the mechanics scale down:

  • Prove demand before you set the price. Take-Two opened pre-orders on June 25, 2026, almost five months before launch, and used the response to talk about the year with confidence. If your launch depends on people who already raised their hand, build that list first; a lead generation program that collects and follows up interest gives you a number to price against.
  • Offer a ladder, not one price. $79.99, $99.99 and a $20 upgrade later lets buyers start low and move up when they are already committed.
  • Put a date on the bonus. The Vintage Vice City Pack only comes with purchases before November 20, 2026, which pulls buying forward.
  • Budget the launch spend. Take-Two expects quarterly operating expenses to rise about 21%, mainly for GTA 6 marketing. A premium price needs a visible reason.
  • Define your numbers. Take-Two publishes its Net Bookings definition every quarter. Say what you count before you announce a record.

What to do now

  • If you write or post about GTA 6 money, quote Take-Two's guidance and label analyst numbers as forecasts with a name and date.
  • If you sell around launch day, plan offers for November 19, 2026 and the weekend after, and do not rely on discs: there are none in the box.
  • If you price your own product, test a premium tier and an upgrade path before you raise the base price.
  • Watch for Take-Two's report on the quarter ending December 31, 2026. It is the first scheduled report that covers launch.

faqs: How much money will GTA 6 make?

Take-Two does not publish a GTA 6-only figure. It expects $8.0 to $8.2 billion in Net Bookings for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, up from $6.72 billion, and $3.35 to $3.5 billion for October to December 2026, against $1.76 billion a year earlier. Analysts' unit forecasts, such as Brian Pitz of BMO Capital Markets forecasting 55 million copies in that fiscal year, as GameSpot reported on November 13, 2026, are forecasts, not results.
How much money has GTA 6 made in pre-orders?

Take-Two has not disclosed a pre-order number. On November 9, 2026 it said pre-orders were tracking far in excess of its initial expectations, and its finance chief called the level extraordinary, but it gave no units or dollars.

The standard edition is $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition is $99.99 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The Xbox Store also sells an Ultimate Edition Upgrade for $20.00 for owners of the standard edition. The physical box holds a download code, not a disc.
Did GTA 5 make $1 billion in 3 days?

In retail sales, yes, by Take-Two's own estimate; that is what buyers paid, not Take-Two's revenue. On September 20, 2013 it said Grand Theft Auto V reached more than $1 billion in worldwide retail sales in its first three days. In November 2026 it said the game has sold nearly 235 million units.
How much did GTA 6 cost to make?
Take-Two has not disclosed a development or marketing budget for GTA 6. It has said operating expenses for October to December 2026 should rise about 21%, mainly because of marketing for the launch.

Net Bookings is Take-Two's operating measure: the net amount of products and services sold digitally or sold-in to stores in a period, including licensing, merchandise and in-game advertising. For PlayStation, Xbox and Steam sales, Take-Two's 10-K says it reports revenue based on what it receives from the store, not the price the player pays.
